name: Yang Ying
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Yang Ying is a director of Chinese drugmaker Xiamen Amoytop Biotech.
Founded in 1996, Amoytop supplies recombinant protein drugs.
Yang's husband Lan Chun is the company's chairman; the two are investors.

name: Myron Wentz
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: Myron Wentz is the founder of USANA, a multilevel marketing company that sells nutritional supplements and skincare products.
Wentz owns 40% of the $850 million (net sales) business, which trades on the NYSE. He took it public in 1996.
In December 2019, he retired as USANA's chairman.
Prior to USANA, he founded Gull Laboratories in 1974 to sell diagnostic tests to hospitals and labs; he sold his stake in 1994 for $22 million.
Wentz renounced his American citizenship in the mid-1990s. He now claims citizenship in tax haven St. Kitts & Nevis.
forbes_facts: Wentz spends most of his time at Sanoviv Medical Institute, a holistic care center he founded in 1998 in Rosarito, Mexico.
Wentz enjoys snorkeling and watching coral reef videos on YouTube.

name: Weijian Shan
forbes_bio: Weijian Shan is the chairman of PAG, an Asia-focused private equity firm with $50 billion in assets under management.
Before founding PAG's private equity business in 2010, he worked for 12 years at TPG Capital and was the U.S. private equity giant's top China dealmaker.
At TPG, Shan spearheaded the first purchase of a state-owned Chinese bank by a foreign investor.
In 2022, Shan became an independent director of Alibaba. He also served on the boards of Wilmar International, Bank of China (Hong Kong), Baosteel and Lenovo.
forbes_facts: The Beijing-born grew up during the Cultural Revolution and labored in northern China's Gobi Desert.
His memoir, published in 2019, is called Out of the Gobi: My Story of China and America.
He earned a Ph.D. in business administration from UC Berkeley, where U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen was one of Shan's thesis advisors.

name: Alexander Mikhalskiy
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Alexander Mikhalskiy is a cofounder of Sportmaster, Russia's largest sports and fashion retailer, which he started with brothers Nikolay and Vladimir Fartushnyak.
He also cofounded Ostin, a Russian fast-fashion retailer, with the brothers, both of whom are billionaires.
In the early 1990s Mikhalskiy and his partners had a distribution business that supplied French consumer goods to the Russian market.
They later became the exclusive distributor for German sports retailer Kettler and opened the first Sportmaster store in 1997.

name: Arno Schodl
forbes_bio: Arno Schodl co-founded think-cell, a German software company, along with his partner Markus Hannebauer.
The partners founded the business in 2002, growing to more than 50,000 users and winning the Berlin Startup award for that year.
Schodl holds a Phd with a specialization in computer graphics and shares a 30% stake in the company along with Hannebauer.
Think-cell, which sold a majority stake to PE firm Cinven in 2021, specializes data visualization tools for the creation of PowerPoint presentations.

name: Xie Juhua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Xie Juhua is a director and the largest individual shareholder at Kingfriend, a pharmaceuticals supplier.
Kingfriend's main products include cardiovascular and anti-tumor drugs.
Xie's son Tang Yongqun chairs Kingfriend.

name: Jan Van Geet
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Jan Van Geet is the founder and CEO of VGP, a Belgian real estate company.
VGP specializes in developing industrial office parks, with properties in 12 European countries.
Van Geet founded the company in 1998 in the former Czech Republic.
He currently owns about a third of the publicly-traded company, which listed its shares in 2007.
A passionate equestrian, his hobby is dressage.

name: Anton Rabie
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2018-2022); Hurun Global (2018-2019); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Anton Rabie is the cofounder and co-CEO of Spin Master Corp., known for its popular kids' toys like Hatchimals, Air Hogs and Paw Patrol.
Rabie started the company in 1994 with childhood friend Ronnen Harary.
Armed with $10,000, Rabie and Harary released Spin Master's first toy in 1994. It was called "Earth Buddy" and resembled a Chia Pet.
Spin Master had its IPO in 2015.
Spin Master is now a $1.6 billion (sales) company, which employs over 1,500 people in 16 countries.
forbes_facts: Rabie and Harary reportedly met at summer camp in Ontario when they were both 11 years old.
Spin Master made toys for the popular children's TV show, The Wiggles.
In 2021, Spin Master acquired the Rubik's cube for $50 million.

name: Ashok Boob
forbes_bio: Ashok Boob gets his wealth from his holding in specialty chemicals maker Clean Science and Technology.
The Pune company made a stellar debut on the stock market in July 2021, listing at a 98% premium.
The bulk of the company's $70 million revenue comes from specialty chemicals that are used in everything from infant food formulas to cosmetics to cereals.
It also makes pharma intermediaries which are used in cough syrups and anti-retrovirals.
Boob is the cofounder and managing director.
